It works, but only with a tidy exit. Wednesday: breakfast at 6:30 leaves plenty of time for the 7:45 coffee. Thursday: if debrief ends 12:45, get the bag by 1:05, rideshare 1:10, CVG about 1:40-1:50 in rain; that’s 85-95 minutes before departure with carry-on only.
What’s the later flight cost?
Later option I see: United CVG-ORD 5:35-5:59, about +$86 fare difference. It adds comfort if the debrief drifts past 1:00, but also means killing extra time at CVG and getting home around dinner.
Keep the current one unless you think the margin is irresponsible.
I’d keep the 3:15 for now. Set a firm 12:45 stop, order the rideshare while walking back to Hampton, and skip checking a bag. Change only if the host warns the debrief could go past 1:00.

messages.content: Cincinnati is wrapped. I need to start Atlanta for the grantmaker forum, Nov. 15-17. Welcome reception the first evening in Midtown, full-day meeting Wednesday near the arts center, and a Thursday committee breakfast that should end around 11:30. I want to fly from Chicago, avoid renting a car, and get back Thursday after lunch without landing really late.

Got it. I’ll compare flight-and-hotel pairings rather than just flights. A couple of details first: one traveler in economy, and are both ORD and MDW acceptable? Also, should I use the forum hotel block as one option even if breakfast is not included?

One traveler, economy, carry-on only. ORD is easier, but MDW is okay if it’s a clear savings. Please include the block hotel and at least one nearby lower-rate place with breakfast. I’d like the lodging total to be defensible for reimbursement, not luxury.
Do you need to arrive before the reception with much buffer, or is landing around mid-afternoon fine? And should all hotel options be refundable at this stage?
Landing by about 4:30 is fine. Refundable for now. Standard one-bed room is fine, and I’d rather not be stuck somewhere without an easy dinner option after the reception.

Here are the strongest current pairings, using two nights and estimated airport rideshares in the trip total. Fares and rates should be rechecked before booking.

| Pairing | Flights | Hotel | Est. total | Meeting access | Breakfast / room basics | Dining + cancellation |
|---|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| A: Block + United | ORD-ATL 11:50a-2:43p; ATL-ORD 2:15p-3:23p | Hotel Midtown Atlanta, forum block, $214/nt; est. $506 all-in | $868 | 3-4 min walk to arts center | Breakfast not included; room lists coffee maker + mini-fridge | On-site restaurant/bar, Colony Square nearby; block cancel shown to Nov. 11, verify at checkout |
| B: Hampton + United | Same United flights | Hampton Inn & Suites Atlanta-Midtown, $166/nt; est. $395 all-in | $757 | 7-9 min walk, close to Arts Center MARTA | Breakfast included; room lists coffee maker, mini-fridge, microwave | No full-service restaurant, but several dinner spots within a few blocks; cancel to Nov. 13 |
| C: Hyatt Centric + Delta | ORD-ATL 12:35p-3:34p; ATL-ORD 2:55p-4:04p | Hyatt Centric Midtown, $189/nt; est. $450 all-in | $777 | 12-15 min walk or short rideshare | Breakfast not included; coffee + mini-fridge listed | On-site restaurant; cancel to Nov. 12 |
Is MARTA realistic from the airport with a rollaboard, or should I assume rideshares?

MARTA is realistic for the Midtown options. Airport to Arts Center or Midtown station is usually about 25-30 minutes on the train, $2.50 each way, then a short walk. Rideshare is simpler with a tired arrival: roughly $35-$45 each way depending on traffic. No rental car looks reasonable either way.
Can you verify whether the block includes breakfast? I don’t want to assume.

The block rate does not show included breakfast. It shows paid breakfast/coffee options on property, plus in-room coffee and a mini-fridge. Hampton is the only one in the shortlist clearly listing breakfast included.
Can you reframe the totals without airport rideshares, assuming MARTA unless I arrive too tired?

Sure. With MARTA instead of rideshares, the trip totals drop by about $71.

| Option | Air + hotel + MARTA | Arrival / return fit | Practical trade-off |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Block + United | about $797 | Best return: 2:15 p.m. after the 11:30 breakfast | Most convenient walks; paid breakfast makes mornings pricier |
| Hampton + United | about $686 | Same good return timing | Saves about $111 before breakfast value; slightly longer walks |
| Hyatt + Delta | about $706 | Later return, still not late | Cheaper flight, but no breakfast and farther from the arts center |
So Hampton saves a little over $100 against the block, before counting breakfast?

Yes. With the same United flights, Hampton is about $111 less on room cost. If you would otherwise buy two breakfasts or coffee-and-a-light-bite, the practical savings are closer to $135-$150. The trade-off is losing the shortest walk and the full-service hotel lobby/restaurant feel.
What if I use Delta instead of United? I’m fine with either if the timing is better.

Delta is about $35 less right now, but the return leaves around 2:55 p.m. and gets to Chicago closer to 4:00. United costs a bit more but gives you an earlier home arrival and still departs after lunch. Since the Thursday breakfast should end at 11:30, both work; United is the smoother return, Delta is the small savings.
Let’s not ticket airfare until I confirm whether the reception is actually at the block hotel. Which hotel would you hold if I need one today?

If the reception stays centered at the block hotel, I’d hold the block for maximum convenience. If the reception is just somewhere in Midtown, I’d hold Hampton: lower total, breakfast included, practical room setup, and still walkable to the arts center. The key question is whether the block’s location saves you any evening transportation.
Please save the block and Hampton as finalists, no booking yet. I’ll ask the organizer about the reception location.

Saved. Finalists are Hotel Midtown Atlanta in the forum block and Hampton Inn & Suites Atlanta-Midtown. No hotel held and no airfare ticketed yet. Working flight shortlist: United for the earlier return, Delta for modest savings. Next step is to confirm the reception location before the block deadline.

messages.content: Atlanta update: the organizer confirmed the Wednesday session stays near the arts center, but the Tuesday reception moved to the host museum. The block closes tomorrow morning. Can you help me choose between the block hotel and Hampton before I miss it?
Yes. Is the host museum the same arts-center area, and do you still want to avoid night rideshares if the walk is reasonable? I’ll keep airfare separate since we haven’t ticketed it.

Yes, it’s the museum right by the arts center. I’m fine with a short well-lit walk, but I don’t want a hotel that makes me take extra cars at night. Mornings should be easy. Standard one-bed room, refrigerator confirmed if possible, and either breakfast included or very reliable coffee nearby.

Here’s the narrowed hotel comparison for Nov. 15-17:

| Hotel | Est. 2-night total | Access | Breakfast / coffee | Room basics | Dinner + terms |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Hotel Midtown Atlanta, forum block | about $506 | Shortest: 3-4 min walk to museum/arts center | Not included; paid cafe/restaurant | Standard king/queen rooms list coffee maker + mini-fridge | On-site restaurant/bar; block closes tomorrow, cancel shown to Nov. 11 |
| Hampton Inn & Suites Atlanta-Midtown | about $395 | 5-8 min walk to museum/arts center; close to Arts Center MARTA | Breakfast included; lobby coffee listed | Standard one-bed room lists mini-fridge, microwave, coffee maker | No full-service restaurant, but several nearby dinner options; cancel to Nov. 13 |
Is the Hampton walk okay after an evening reception, or is that savings false economy?

It looks reasonable rather than false economy. The Hampton is still in the arts-center/Midtown cluster, not a different neighborhood. You give up the block lobby convenience, but you should not need an extra rideshare just to get back after the museum reception.
And the Hampton room actually has the refrigerator? That’s the one detail I don’t want to chase later.

The available Hampton standard one-bed room lists a mini-fridge, microwave, and coffee maker. I’d still put a note on the reservation to confirm mini-fridge and request a quiet room away from the elevator.
Which one would you hold?

I’d hold Hampton. It saves about $111 on the room total, includes breakfast, keeps you close enough to both the reception and Wednesday session, and has the room basics you asked about. The block is only worth the premium if most networking is happening in that hotel.
Okay, hold Hampton refundable, one queen if available, quiet room, refrigerator note. Do not ticket airfare yet.
I can do that. I won’t book the block hotel. If the Hampton queen room is unavailable at the quoted rate, should I use a standard king instead rather than lose the refundable rate?
Yes, king is fine if queen disappears. Please hold it and keep the United and Delta flight shortlist.

Held Hampton Inn & Suites Atlanta-Midtown for Nov. 15-17, refundable standard one-bed room; queen requested, king acceptable if the hotel assigns that bedding. Estimated total is $395 with taxes. Notes added: quiet room away from elevator and mini-fridge confirmation. Breakfast is included, in-room coffee is listed, and the hotel remains walkable to the museum/arts-center meetings. No airfare ticketed; United and Delta remain the flight shortlist.
